items.figure: Half-adder: connect inputs A and B to an XOR gate for Sum S and an AND gate for Carry C. Full-adder: connect A, B and Cin to a three-input XOR gate for Sum S. For Carry Cout, connect A and B, A and Cin, and B and Cin to three AND gates, then connect their outputs to an OR gate.
steps: A half-adder adds two binary digits, A and B. It produces a Sum (S) and a Carry (C).
Half-adder truth table:
A | B | S | C
Half-adder Boolean expressions: S = A ⊕ B; C = A · B.
A full-adder adds three binary digits: A, B and the input carry Cin. It produces a Sum (S) and an output carry (Cout).
Full-adder truth table:
A | B | Cin | S | Cout
Full-adder Boolean expressions: S = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin; Cout = A · B + A · Cin + B · Cin.
A half-adder has no carry input, so it is used when there is no carry from a previous column, such as the least significant bit.
A full-adder accepts a carry input and is used for the other columns of a multi-bit addition.
items.finalAnswer: A half-adder adds two bits and has no carry input; a full-adder adds two bits and an input carry. Their outputs are given by the truth tables and Boolean expressions above.

items.figure: Draw a three-variable Karnaugh map with columns AB in Gray-code order 00, 01, 11, 10 and rows C = 0, 1. Enter 1 in the cells for minterms 1, 3, 5 and 7. The four 1s fill the entire C = 1 row; group them together and label the group C.
steps: A Karnaugh map (K-map) is a graphical method for simplifying Boolean expressions. Each cell represents one minterm.
Arrange the cells in Gray-code order so that adjacent cells differ in only one variable. Place a 1 in each cell where the function is 1.
Make the largest possible rectangular groups of adjacent 1s. The group size must be a power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on. The first and last cells of a row or column are also adjacent.
For each group, keep only the variables that remain unchanged within that group. Remove variables that change. OR the resulting terms to obtain the simplified expression.
Example: Simplify F(A, B, C) = Σm(1, 3, 5, 7).
Use columns AB in Gray-code order 00, 01, 11, 10 and rows C = 0, 1.
K-map:
The four 1s in the C = 1 row form one group of four.
Within this group, A and B change, so they are eliminated. C remains 1 throughout the group.
Therefore, F = C.
items.finalAnswer: A K-map simplifies a Boolean expression by grouping adjacent 1s and retaining only the variables that remain unchanged; in the example, F = C.

items.figure: Draw four stages from right to left. Connect A0 and B0 to a half-adder; label its outputs S0 and C1. Connect A1, B1 and C1 to a full-adder; label its outputs S1 and C2. Connect A2, B2 and C2 to a full-adder; label its outputs S2 and C3. Connect A3, B3 and C3 to a full-adder; label its outputs S3 and C4. The result is C4 S3 S2 S1 S0.
steps: To add two 4-bit numbers A3A2A1A0 and B3B2B1B0, connect the adders in order from the least significant bit (bit 0) to the most significant bit (bit 3).
At bit 0, there is no input carry. Use a half-adder with inputs A0 and B0.
Half-adder truth table:
A | B | S | C
Half-adder expressions: S0 = A0 ⊕ B0; C1 = A0 · B0.
At bit 1, use a full-adder with inputs A1, B1 and carry C1. Its outputs are S1 and C2.
At bit 2, use a full-adder with inputs A2, B2 and carry C2. Its outputs are S2 and C3.
At bit 3, use a full-adder with inputs A3, B3 and carry C3. Its outputs are S3 and final carry C4.
Full-adder truth table:
A | B | Cin | S | Cout
At each full-adder: Si = Ai ⊕ Bi ⊕ Ci; Ci+1 = Ai · Bi + Ai · Ci + Bi · Ci.
The 5-bit result is C4S3S2S1S0. C4 is the final carry and is included when the addition produces an overflow beyond four bits.
items.finalAnswer: Use one half-adder for bit 0 and three full-adders for bits 1, 2 and 3; the 5-bit sum is C4S3S2S1S0.

steps: F(A, B) = A · B + A · B̅
Take A as the common factor: F = A · (B + B̅).
By the complement law, B + B̅ = 1.
Therefore, F = A · 1 = A.
By De Morgan’s law, (A + B)̅ = A̅ · B̅ and (A · C)̅ = A̅ + C̅.
Therefore, F = A̅ · B̅ + A̅ + C̅.
By the absorption law, A̅ + A̅ · B̅ = A̅.
Therefore, F = A̅ + C̅.
Let X = A + B. Then the expression is X̅ · X.
By the complement law, X̅ · X = 0.
Therefore, (A + B)̅ · (A + B) = 0.
Using the identity (X + Y) · (X + Z) = X + Y · Z:
By the complement law, B̅ · B = 0.
Therefore, A + 0 = A.
Using the distributive law, A + A̅ · X = (A + A̅) · (A + X), where X = B̅ + C.
Therefore, A + A̅ · (B̅ + C) = (A + A̅) · (A + B̅ + C).
By the complement law, A + A̅ = 1.
Therefore, 1 · (A + B̅ + C) = A + B̅ + C.
